Visible by handle until %1$s. Older app versions and anyone who knows your handle can find you; every such window can be linked to the others.
Turn on rotating discovery IDs first. Without them this phone is always visible by handle.

On by default. While you are ready for calls or sharing a stream, this phone broadcasts a new random ID every 15 minutes instead of its fixed ID, so a scanner cannot follow it from place to place. Other phones see \"Nearby phone\" and learn who you are only when they connect; anyone who connects still learns that. Verified contacts who allow it can recognise you nearby (shown as unconfirmed). On Android 14 and newer it also hides this phone\'s Bluetooth name from phones that connect without being paired; on older Android the name stays readable (this does not rename your phone; see the option below). Older versions of the app cannot see this phone or be seen by it, and joining a stream from an older phone shows your fixed ID while you join. Older versions can find your streams for a while with \"Visible by handle\"; they cannot call you while \"Pseudonymous toward strangers\" is on. Phones paired with this one in Android settings can always recognise it. Takes effect the next time this phone gets ready for calls or starts a stream.
This phone\'s Bluetooth chip may keep its address when the ID changes, so a scanner nearby could still link your IDs. Rotating IDs protect less on this phone.

Off by default. Any phone that connects to you can read this phone\'s Bluetooth name before any security check, and headphones, cars and other phones show it too. On: the name becomes \"Phone\" for everything on this phone (headphones, car, watch, PC, Quick Share) and turning this off puts your name back. If you uninstall the app while this is on, the name stays \"Phone\" until you rename the phone in Android settings.

This renames your phone for everything: headphones, your car, your watch, PCs and Quick Share will show \"Phone\". Your name now: %1$s. Turn this option off to get it back. If you uninstall the app while it is on, the name stays \"Phone\" until you rename the phone in Android settings.

Without rotating discovery IDs the name is readable by phones that connect. Turn them on to hide it on Android 14 and newer, or use this option on any phone.

While rotating discovery IDs are on, phones that connect to you without being paired cannot read the name on this phone. Calls you place and streams you send still show it to the phone you connect to, and Classic Bluetooth lookups see it; this option hides it there too.

Off by default. Lets phones nearby relay private calls for each other, in the background, and lets you call a phone one or two relays away. Relays use the old handshake, so it works only between phones that have \"Pseudonymous toward strangers\" turned off (Settings > Features); with it on, a relayed call to a phone that is not your verified contact fails. A relay carries encrypted calls it cannot read or change, but it can see who is calling whom (public identity keys) and when. Helping pauses below 20% battery (unless charging) and in Battery Saver, and your own calls and streams always come first.
Let phones nearby relay calls to me

Phones up to two relays away will broadcast that you are reachable, so people near them can learn you are within two relays. A helping phone sees public identity keys and call timing, never call content. You can change both choices in Settings.
Ask the other person to open Call on their phone. Stay within about 10 to 30 metres. The list updates by itself.

Hot: 10% less frame rate and quality. Very hot: 20% less. If the phone becomes dangerously hot, video stops even when this is off.

Your identity, verified contacts, messages and settings will be erased now. Other people will see you as a new, unverified person. This cannot be undone.

Off by default. When on, tapping the app name on the home screen three times quickly starts an emergency wipe after a 3-second chance to undo. Use only if you may need to erase fast.

Turn on Manual settings above to change experimental features.
Talk and share video without internet
This app connects phones directly over Bluetooth. It works where there is no mobile signal or Wi-Fi, or where the internet is blocked.
Voice and video calls with people nearby, encrypted from end to end.
Go live for everyone nearby, or watch someone else.

Other phones can carry calls and live video further. A phone that passes on a private call cannot see or hear it. Live video is different: anyone watching it, including a phone that passes it on, can see it.

• No account, no servers, no internet, no analytics.
• Range is about 10 to 30 metres between two phones, less through walls and bodies. Each phone that relays adds another hop.
• Video is small and may pause on a weak link; sound is kept going first.
• Both phones need this app open.
• Tip: before you rely on it, test the range with a friend by walking apart during a call.
Nearby devices: find and connect to other phones.
Location: older Android versions require it for Bluetooth scanning. The app does not read your location.

Off by default. Adds an optional name (Settings, Your ID), a subject when you place a call and a title when you go live. Names and subjects travel only inside the encrypted call, signed by your identity key; a stream title is also advertised publicly so people nearby see it before joining (shown as unconfirmed until they join). Phones without this see only your handle.
Shown to people you call, marked self-named; your handle never changes. Anyone who knows your handle can tell when your phone is nearby with a Bluetooth scanner.
